svg.title: nsdn — overview schematic
svg.text: nsdn — a generic framework for BI with an agentic layer
A proposed design, now being tried in a sandbox. Governed work runs as a chain — proposes → decides → executes → checks — with stages automated where policy allows. Updated 2026-10-08.
its own; none owes a link
set purpose and delegation policy · rule on meaning, disputes and consequences · act on insight
Directly, by mandate: meaning, KPI definitions, priorities, anything irreversible or regulatory.
Everything else is decided within the policy they set. Attention is a fixed weekly budget per role.
They alone change the constitution, and only they may override a gate; every override is recorded.
aims at the most loss averted per minute · most proposals never reach a person
rulings; a ruling on a pattern becomes a precedent
writes and explains: code, templates, metadata, tests, diagnoses — and triages its own proposals
First build: one builder agent, checked by a second model that works out keys and grain again on its own.
Approval is tied to one commit: any change to its inputs voids it, and the gates run again.
More roles (coordinator, planner, tester …) are added only when the step log shows they pay.
in git, as text · the rulebook and the code
constitution: fixed principles, changed only by people
mission brief per build · playbooks per role
warehouse code and data model as
each release with a note: what changed,
why, and its expected effect on output
Agents work only from the rules written here; they may propose changes, people decide.
dashed green: one identity plane over every store, data platform and context alike — access is filtered before anything is retrieved, by people or agents
run end to end by DETERMINISTIC MACHINERY · no model in the data path
approved rules and definitions feed the mart build
Data Vault or a functionally equivalent layer: all data, all history, integrated on business keys.
Rule versioning and lineage: any past report can be reproduced.
Temporal behaviour and join knowledge are measured here, and tested before anything relies on them.
Three gates, run by the machinery, not by agents
Change gate: code reaches the machinery only when its tests pass.
Load & publication gate: a mart version is published only when its tests pass. Plausibility checks warn;
an error of ten times or more against like-for-like blocks publication until someone looks.
Semantic admission: an approved rule or definition starts feeding marts only through this gate.
Tests are sorted by root cause. Release regression on frozen data: every change in the output must match a release note.
Keeps running when the agentic layer is down: the checks run on their own schedule and raise their own alerts.
the context system records what is
true about the data; the repository
Built to grow very large while
agents still find their way by
• Mandate is separate from capability; models never operate in the data path; autonomy is tiered.
• Every accepted claim traces to evidence or to a responsible person.
• Where machines can check the output, the agentic layer scales; where only judgement
can check it, people remain the bottleneck.
• Human attention is the scarce resource. Where damage is bounded, reversibility plus
fast detection can substitute for review; more review is not always less risk.
• Cost must not simply move elsewhere. Passing the gates is necessary, not sufficient,
• Generic: the full design is described; an implementation starts lean and adopts each
further stage only once it needs it and its prerequisites work.
• The central bet: can the agentic layer propose business keys well
enough to be worth a person's time to check?
• The economics: cost per proposal, and human minutes of adjudication
per week. Neither is quantified yet.
• What success means for each capability.
• Whether a team of agents does better than one builder agent.
• Under way: a sandbox on a simulated order system (Wide World
Importers), advanced one simulated day at a time. Business owners
and reviewers are simulated there, and results must say so.
